title: Classical Mediterranean Kingdoms (Lydia, Tyre, Carthage/Barcids, Numidia, Pontus, Armenia, Bactria, Seleucids), Alba Longa, 7 Kings of Rome, Roman/Byzantine Emperors & Universal Royal Bridges (Betham 1795, Anderson 1732, Eusebius)

nodes.name: Mermnad Dynasty of Lydia: Gyges → Ardys → Sadyattes → Alyattes → King Croesus
nodes.era: 680-546 BCE (Herodotus I; Eusebius; Betham Tab. LXVI)
nodes.role: Inventors of Coinage & Anatolian Empire Defeated by Cyrus
nodes.notes: Overthrew Heraclid king Candaules (son of Myrsus). Alyattes's daughter Aryenis married Median King Astyages (grandfather of Cyrus the Great!), making Croesus the great-uncle/brother-in-law of the Median court he fought to avenge against Cyrus in 546 BCE.

nodes.name: Kings of Tyre: Abibaal → Hiram I → Baal-ezer → Ethbaal I (Ithobaal) → Mattan I → Pygmalion & Dido
nodes.era: c. 990-774 BCE (Josephus Against Apion I.18; Betham Tab. XCII)
nodes.role: Phoenician Maritime Dynasty Linking Solomon, Ahab & Carthage
nodes.notes: Menander of Ephesus (quoted by Josephus!) preserves the complete Tyrian royal archive: Hiram I (ally of David & Solomon) -> ... -> Ethbaal I (Priest of Astarte, father of Queen Jezebel who married King Ahab of Israel!) -> Baal-ezer II -> Mattan I -> Pygmalion & Princess Elissa/Dido (founder of Carthage, 814 BCE)!

nodes.name: Barcid Dynasty of Carthage: Hamilcar Barca → Hannibal Barca, Hasdrubal & Mago
nodes.notes: Hamilcar Barca (hero of 1st Punic War) fathered Hannibal the Great (crossed the Alps in 218 BCE, victor at Cannae), Hasdrubal Barca, Mago Barca, and daughters married to Hasdrubal the Fair & Numidian prince Naravas. Allied with Hasdrubal Gisco (father of Sophonisba).

nodes.name: Kings of Numidia & Mauretania: Gaia → Masinissa → Micipsa → Jugurtha; Juba I → Juba II (+ Cleopatra Selene II)
nodes.role: Amazigh (Berber) Royal Dynasties of North Africa
nodes.notes: Masinissa unified Numidia (ally of Scipio Africanus against Hannibal); his grandson Jugurtha resisted Rome. Later King Juba II of Mauretania married Cleopatra Selene II (daughter of Mark Antony & Cleopatra VII of Egypt!), fathering King Ptolemy of Mauretania — uniting Berber, Ptolemaic Egyptian, and Roman bloodlines!

nodes.name: Seleucid Empire: Seleucus I Nicator (+ Apama of Sogdia) → Antiochus I → Antiochus III the Great → Antiochus IV Epiphanes
nodes.era: 312-63 BCE (Eusebius Chronicle; Betham Tab. CIII; 1 Maccabees)
nodes.role: Hellenistic Kings of Syria, Mesopotamia & Persia
nodes.notes: Founded by Alexander's general Seleucus I Nicator & Iranian princess Apama (daughter of Spitamenes of Sogdia). Antiochus III the Great's daughter Cleopatra I Syra married Ptolemy V (starting the 'Cleopatra' name in Egypt!). Antiochus IV Epiphanes sparked the Maccabean Revolt (167 BCE).

nodes.name: Antigonid Macedon (Antigonus I, Demetrius, Philip V, Perseus) & Pyrrhus of Epirus
nodes.role: Final Macedonian Kings & Aeacid Kings of Epirus
nodes.notes: Antigonus Monophthalmus -> Demetrius Poliorcetes -> Antigonus II Gonatas -> Philip V -> Perseus (defeated by Rome at Pydna, 168 BCE). King Pyrrhus of Epirus (cousin of Alexander via Olympias & claiming descent from Achilles's son Neoptolemus!) fought Rome ('Pyrrhic victory').

nodes.name: Kingdom of Pontus: Mithridates I Ktistes → Pharnaces I → Mithridates VI Eupator ('The Poison King')
nodes.role: Persian-Greek Royal Dynasty of the Black Sea
nodes.notes: Claimed descent from both Darius the Great (Achaemenids) and Alexander/Seleucids! Mithridates VI Eupator waged three Mithridatic Wars against Rome; his daughter Cleopatra married King Tigranes the Great of Armenia, and his son Pharnaces II ruled the Bosporan Kingdom ('Veni, vidi, vici').

nodes.name: Artaxiad Armenia: Artaxias I → Tigranes II the Great (+ Cleopatra of Pontus) → Artavasdes II & Herodian Tigranes V/VI
nodes.era: 189 BCE – 63 CE (Betham Tab. LXXXIII; Josephus Ant. XVIII)
nodes.role: Imperial Kingdom of Armenia Linking Pontus, Parthia & Judea
nodes.notes: Artaxias I founded Artaxata; Tigranes the Great built a vast empire from the Caspian to the Mediterranean. Remarkable dynastic link: Herod the Great's grandson Tigranes V & great-grandson Tigranes VI (via Alexander + Glaphyra of Cappadocia) were placed on the throne of Armenia by Rome!

nodes.name: Greco-Bactrian & Indo-Greek Kings: Diodotus I → Euthydemus → Demetrius I → Menander I (King Milinda)
nodes.role: Hellenistic Kings of Afghanistan & Northwest India
nodes.notes: Diodotus broke away from the Seleucids in Bactria; Demetrius I invaded India (Gandhara/Punjab); Menander I Soter (Pali: Milinda) converted to Buddhism in the famous dialogue Milinda Panha with sage Nagasena — bridging Greek, Iranian, and Indian civilizations!

nodes.name: Royal Houses of Adiabene (Monobazus I & Queen Helena → Izates II) & Osroene/Edessa (King Abgar V)
nodes.era: 1st c. CE (Josephus Ant. XX.2; Betham Tab. LXX-LXXI)
nodes.role: Upper Mesopotamian Client Kingdoms Famous in Jewish & Syriac History
nodes.notes: Queen Helena of Adiabene & her son King Izates II converted to Judaism (~30 CE), funded famine relief in Jerusalem, and built the monumental Tomb of the Kings in Jerusalem. King Abgar V Ukkama of Edessa (Osroene) features in Syriac chronicles as the first Christian monarch.

nodes.name: Kings of Alba Longa: Ascanius (Iulus) → Silvius → Capys → Tiberinus → Aventinus → Procas → Numitor & Amulius
nodes.era: c. 1177-753 BCE (Livy I; Eusebius Chronicle; Betham Tab. CIX-CXI)
nodes.role: 14 Trojan-Latin Kings Bridging Aeneas to Romulus & Remus
nodes.notes: Complete Latin succession from Aeneas (+ Lavinia daughter of King Latinus): Ascanius/Iulus (claimed ancestor of the Julii Caesars!), Silvius Posthumus, Aeneas Silvius, Latinus Silvius, Alba, Atys, Capys, Capetus, Tiberinus (eponym of the Tiber River), Agrippa, Romulus Silvius, Aventinus, Procas -> Numitor (father of Rhea Silvia) & usurper Amulius.

nodes.name: 7 Kings of Rome: Romulus, Numa Pompilius, Tullus Hostilius, Ancus Marcius, Tarquinius Priscus, Servius Tullius & Tarquinius Superbus
nodes.era: 753-509 BCE (Livy I; Eusebius; Betham Tab. CXII)
nodes.role: Complete Roman Monarchy to Republic Founder L. Junius Brutus
nodes.notes: Sabine co-ruler Titus Tatius -> Numa Pompilius -> Tullus Hostilius -> Ancus Marcius -> Etruscan Tarquinius Priscus (+ Tanaquil) -> Servius Tullius -> Tarquinius Superbus (expelled in 509 BCE by Lucius Junius Brutus & Tarquinius Collatinus, founding the Roman Republic!).

nodes.name: Julio-Claudian Emperors: Augustus (+ Livia) → Tiberius, Caligula, Claudius & Nero
nodes.era: 27 BCE – 68 CE (Suetonius; Tacitus; Betham Tab. CXXI; Anderson)
nodes.role: First Imperial Dynasty of Rome (New Testament Era)
nodes.notes: Augustus (census at Jesus's birth, Luke 2:1) -> Tiberius (Jesus's ministry & crucifixion, Luke 3:1) -> Caligula (descended from Mark Antony & Agrippa) -> Claudius (Acts 18:2) -> Nero (martyrdom of Peter & Paul, Great Fire of 64 CE).

nodes.name: Flavian (Vespasian, Titus, Domitian), Five Good Emperors (Trajan, Hadrian, Marcus Aurelius) & Severan Dynasties
nodes.role: High Imperial Roman Dynasties (Including Syro-Punic Severans)
nodes.notes: Vespasian & Titus (destruction of Jerusalem Temple, 70 CE — patrons of Josephus!) -> Domitian (interviewed grandsons of Jude, brother of Jesus!). Nerva -> Trajan -> Hadrian -> Antoninus Pius -> Marcus Aurelius -> Commodus. Septimius Severus (Punic/Libyan from Leptis Magna!) + Julia Domna (Priest-King house of Emesa!) -> Caracalla.

nodes.name: Constantine the Great → Theodosius I → Justinian I → Heraclius → Basil I → Alexios Komnenos → Constantine XI
nodes.role: Christian Roman & Eastern Byzantine Imperial Lineages
nodes.notes: Constantine I (+ St. Helena) founded Constantinople (330 CE) -> Theodosius I (split East/West 395 CE) -> Justinian I (+ Empress Theodora, Hagia Sophia) -> Heraclius (defeated Sasanian Khosrow II) -> Macedonian Dynasty (Basil I, Basil II) -> Komnenoi -> Palaiologoi (until 1453).

nodes.name: Merovingians (Merovech → Clovis I) & Carolingians (Charles Martel → Pepin → Charlemagne)
nodes.role: Frankish Kings & Founder of the Holy Roman Empire (Ancestral Hub of Europe)
nodes.notes: Clovis I unified the Franks (481-511). Carolingian Mayor of the Palace Charles Martel (Battle of Tours, 732) -> Pepin the Short -> Charlemagne (crowned Emperor 800 CE) -> Louis the Pious -> Treaty of Verdun (Lothair, Louis the German, Charles the Bald). Chroniclers (Fredegar/Anderson) linked early Franks back to Trojan exiles (Francus)!

nodes.name: House of Wessex (Cerdic → Egbert → Alfred the Great → Æthelstan) & Normans (Rollo → William the Conqueror)
nodes.role: Founders of England (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle Bridges Woden → Sceaf of Noah's Ark!)
nodes.notes: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (under King Æthelwulf, father of Alfred the Great) famously traces Wessex back through Cerdic -> Woden (Odin) -> Geat -> Sceaf ('born in Noah's Ark'!) -> Noah -> Adam! Rollo the Viking founded Normandy -> William the Conqueror (1066) -> Henry II & Eleanor of Aquitaine (Plantagenets).

nodes.name: Viking & Slavic Founders: Ragnar Lodbrok, Harald Fairhair (Norway) & Prince Rurik → Vladimir the Great (Kievan Rus')
nodes.notes: Harald Fairhair (Yngling descendant) unified Norway (~872); Varangian Prince Rurik founded Novgorod (862) -> Igor & St. Olga -> Sviatoslav I -> Vladimir the Great (Christianized Kievan Rus', 988, marrying Byzantine princess Anna Porphyrogenita!) -> Yaroslav the Wise (whose daughters became Queens of France, Norway & Hungary!).

nodes.name: Qusayy → Hashim → Abd al-Muttalib → Prophet Muhammad (570–632 CE) → Fatimah & Ali, Umayyads & Abbasids
nodes.era: c. 400-1258 CE (Ibn Ishaq; Al-Biruni; Anderson 1732 Tables 157-158)
nodes.role: Quraysh Banu Hashim Lineage & Early Islamic Caliphates
nodes.notes: Through Adnan -> Fihr (Quraysh) -> Qusayy -> Abd Manaf -> Hashim -> Abd al-Muttalib -> Abdullah & Aminah -> Prophet Muhammad (founder of Islam). Through daughter Fatimah & cousin Ali ibn Abi Talib: Hasan & Husayn (Alids/Hashemites). Through Abd Manaf's son Abd Shams: Umayyad Caliphate (Mu'awiya I, Damascus & Cordoba). Through uncle Al-Abbas: Abbasid Caliphate (Al-Saffah, Harun al-Rashid of Baghdad!).
